- Channel 1 (moving objects): weights are large across rows 2â7, e.g. `(r4,c3)=17.41`, `(r3,c1)=14.07`, `(r4,c1)=15.48`, `(r6,c3)=16.28`. This looks like a ball moving through the playfield.  
- Channel 2 (reward targets): weights are large only in rows 1â3, e.g. `(r3,c1)=6.06`, `(r3,c7)=6.20`, `(r2,c7)=3.68`, `(r1,c6)=2.97`. This suggests static reward targets at the top, i.e. bricks.

Up/down/no-op columns are often similar. Biases are `no-op 1.221, up 1.008, down 1.024, left 0.897, right 1.298`. This means the policy mainly chooses horizontal movement.

The combination of a bottom-row agent, horizontal-only control, a moving ball, static targets in the top rows, and no internal obstacles is the signature of Breakout. Pong is ruled out because its paddle is vertical and the relevant actions would be up/down. Pac-Man, Snake, Sokoban, and similar maze games are ruled out because they would show internal obstacle structure and agent movement throughout the grid. Space Invaders is ruled out because it would have moving reward targets and internal bunkers. Frogger would require upward movement and moving hazards across rows.

Description: The agent controls a paddle on the bottom row, moving left and right to bounce a ball upward and destroy bricks in the top rows; reward comes from hitting or destroying bricks, and the episode ends if the ball passes the paddle.
